name: stage3-machinery-walls-material-v1
title: Stage 3 machinery walls: generated material layering over the v1 categorical keys
state: predicted-static; import only after live capture confirms the key (validate_predicted.py confirm + gate on the AQ-03 Stage 3 capture)
method:
W7-STAGE3 material layering (lane-s3) on the frozen machinery-wall keys (facade-v3 s2c_material_layering method,
adapted to CLUT-indexed atlas pages).

Input: frozen/stage3-machinery-walls-v1 (categorical index-master renders, exact native colours, exact classes) and the
generated tileable swatches in swatches/ (s3_swatches.py, JuggernautXL txt2img, luminance only).
Material maps (CLUT-free, per page, deterministic from the swatches and the inferred cells):
  * every inferred cell gets its own crop of each swatch, made periodic over the cell bbox (offset cross-fade), so a cell
    that the game tiles side by side has no material seam; swatch scale 1:1 at 8 px/texel (1024 px = 128 texels/repeat,
    the facade-v3 world scale);
  * bands: high-pass = blur(fine_sigma) - blur(hp_sigma) (fine wear, scratches; nothing below fine_sigma, so no
    sub-texel shimmer), low-pass = blur(lp_sigma) (mottling), wrap-around filtering inside the cell period.
Per key (CLUT-specific weights from the key's own rendered colour, recomputed for any CLUT):
  log factor = (1 - w_light) * [ (1 - w_paint) * steel(hp, lp) + w_paint * chipped_paint(hp, lp) - grime ]
  w_light: bright saturated or very bright colours (lamps, LEDs, indicator lights) get no material;
  w_paint: saturated paint (hazard stripes, red/orange paint) gets the chipped-paint swatch, neutral steel the steel one;
  grime: oily-grime low-pass, plus darkening in recesses (pixels darker than their 1.5-texel surround: cavity term).
Per cell the material factor is energy-locked (mean visible luminance equals the v1 render, 0.98-1.02), RGB only; the
alpha (class) channel is untouched, then forced and validated at every native texel centre on export (s3master.export).
Nothing is invented: no geometry, glyph, colour or text is added; generated imagery enters only as luminance detail.
usage: python -I s3_material.py [freeze]      -> staging/ or frozen/stage3-machinery-walls-material-v1

review.note: native | v1 categorical | material: full page at 2 px/texel, a 12x crop and a 64x64 window at 9 screen px per texel (2160-line in-game size) labelled SIMULATION. alias_simulation: no-mip bilinear vs area-filtered reference, mean abs luminance error over 8 sub-pixel shifts at 0.5x and 0.33x minification (SIMULATION; higher = more shimmer in motion). No live frame exists for Stage 3.

material_master: material/ holds the swatches, graphs and ComfyUI history; with params + per-cell placement (pages.*.cells) and builder-snapshot/s3_material.py.txt the CLUT-free maps rebuild exactly
known_limits: predicted keys only (no Stage 3 capture); see the base manifest

material is periodic per INFERRED cell: where one inferred cell is really several drawn rects, a rect that the game tiles can show a faint material seam; rebuild per real UV rect after AQ-03 (CPU only, deterministic)
paint/steel/light weights come from each key's rendered colour, so a mispaired CLUT gets material for its own colours
the dithering and line-beading of the v1 categorical base are unchanged underneath the material
honest_read: Inspected the staging sheets v1-vs-material 01-06 (2026-11-13, lane-s3). What it does: large flat panels lose some of the v1 "smooth plastic" look. They get faint oily mottling, fine pitting, and darker recesses from the cavity term. Red and orange paint gets a faint crackle and mottle (from the chipped_paint swatch). Lights and indicator colours stay clean. Brightness is held per cell (energy 0.994-1.004). Colours stay on-palette in hue; texel-centre RGB moves by a median of 2 levels (p95 at most 11). Classes are exact (50 files, 0 mismatches). Honest limits: (1) at the 9 px/texel in-game SIMULATION the change is small, and on busy greeble areas it reads partly as grain/noise rather than as material. (2) The grain is uniform: it does not follow the forms beyond the cavity darkening. (3) It cannot fix what the v1 base gets wrong: rounded shapes, beaded 1-texel lines and blob-smoothed dither all stay. (4) Motion SIMULATION (no-mip bilinear vs area reference): shimmer error is 8-23 % higher than v1 at 0.5x and 5-14 % higher at 0.33x. It is still 50-65 % lower than the stock nearest texture at 0.5x and 5-12 % lower at 0.33x. Verdict: a modest improvement over v1 on flat panels and an improvement over stock, not a true HD surface. Offered as an alternative candidate to v1 (supersedes nothing). Pick v1 or this one after a live look.
